title: Third effect: present fitness for heaven lost in mortal guilt—not by lighter faults under grace
source_text: LIII. Denique docet tertium effectum peccati mortalis esse, quod homo justificatus, quum ejus reatum contrahit, praesentem aptitudinem ad ingrediendum regnum coelo-rum amittat: quoniam in illud regnum non intrabit aliquid coinquinatum, aut abo-minationem faciens: & coelestis corona non imponitur nisi iis qui bonum certamen certarunt, & cursum suum in fide & sanctitate consummarunt, adeoque ineptus est ad hanc coronam adeundam quiquis impietatis operibus adhuc adhaerescit. Quamvis autem peccata quaelibet quantumvis levia exclusionem e regno coelesti, ex justitiae rigore mereantur, tamen juxta providentiae divinae administrationem sub foedere gratiae, peccata istius generis praesentem aptitudinem ad coeleste illud regnum ingre-diendum non tollunt: Sed si mors hominem in hujusmodi tantum peccato depre-hendat, non propterea coelo excluditur, & privatur aeterna gloria & beatitudine.
pass_a_gloss: Finally he teaches that the third effect of mortal sin is that the justified man, when he contracts its guilt, loses present fitness for entering the kingdom of heaven: since nothing defiled, or working abomination, shall enter into that kingdom: and the heavenly crown is not imposed except on those who have fought the good fight and finished their course in faith and holiness, and so whoever still clings to works of impiety is unfit to approach this crown. Although however any sins however light merit exclusion from the heavenly kingdom by the rigor of justice, yet according to the administration of divine providence under the covenant of grace, sins of that lighter kind do not take away present fitness for entering that heavenly kingdom: But if death overtake a man only in a sin of that sort, he is not on that account excluded from heaven and deprived of eternal glory and blessedness.
pass_b_english: Third mortal effect: present kingdom-fitness is lost while defilement and unfinished course remain.
Under grace’s providence, lighter faults alone do not strip that fitness—even if death finds someone only in them.

choices.english: is not on that account excluded from heaven
choices.why: Death in lighter fault ≠ automatic exclusion.
